about

I enjoy transforming raw security telemetry into actionable detections. My passion lies in understanding attacker behavior and building scalable detection capabilities before threats become incidents.

Currently working as a SOC Engineer at NETOPIA, I lead advanced SOC monitoring, detection engineering, and incident response. I specialize in identifying detection blind spots, tuning Sigma/YARA rules, and automating SOC workflows using Python and AI to accelerate MTTD/MTTR.

Active participant in CTFs and hackathons with a strong analytical, critical, and logical mindset. I respond quickly to incidents and am highly motivated to learn, grow, and contribute within dynamic teams.

"Protecting the invisible, securing what matters most. Ready to take on your cyber challenges."

DCSync Detection
MITRE ATT&CK: T1003.006
Detect adversarial use of DCSync to extract credentials from Domain Controllers.
# Sigma rule for DCSync logsource: product: windows service: security detection: selection: EventID: 4662 ObjectType: 'DS-Replication-Get-Changes' condition: selection
SigmaElastic SplunkAtomic Red Team
Kerberoasting Detection
MITRE ATT&CK: T1558.003
Identify Kerberoasting attempts where attackers request TGS tickets for service accounts.
# Sigma rule for Kerberoasting logsource: product: windows service: security detection: selection: EventID: 4769 TicketEncryptionType: '0x17' ServiceName: '*$' condition: selection
SigmaKQLSplunk
PowerShell Download Cradle
MITRE ATT&CK: T1059.001
Detect PowerShell one-liners that download and execute payloads from the internet.
# Sigma rule for PowerShell Download Cradle logsource: product: windows service: powershell detection: keywords: - 'Invoke-WebRequest' - 'Net.WebClient' - 'DownloadString' - 'IEX' condition: keywords
SigmaElasticSysmon
Scheduled Tasks Persistence
MITRE ATT&CK: T1053.005
Detect creation of scheduled tasks as a persistence mechanism.

LOLBins Execution
MITRE ATT&CK: T1218
Detect execution of living-off-the-land binaries used for defense evasion.

SigmaSysmonEDR

threat hunting

Proactive hunts — hypotheses, data sources, and findings.

Kerberos Brute Force

"Attackers may brute force Kerberos TGT requests to discover valid credentials."
Data: Windows Security logs (EventID 4768)
MITRE: T1110.002
Queries: KQL, SPL, Elastic
Findings: Detected 3 anomalous IPs with > 100 failed TGT requests in 5 minutes.

Beaconing Detection

"Compromised hosts may exhibit periodic beaconing to C2 infrastructure."
Data: Proxy logs, DNS logs, Firewall logs
MITRE: T1071
Queries: SPL, Elastic, KQL
Findings: Identified 2 hosts with regular outbound connections to suspicious domains.

Lateral Movement via PsExec

"Attackers may use PsExec for lateral movement across the network."
Data: Sysmon, Windows Security (EventID 4688)
MITRE: T1021.002
Queries: Sigma, Elastic, SPL
Findings: Detected PsExec execution patterns from a non-admin workstation.

incident response

Real investigations — timeline, IOCs, TTPs, and lessons learned.

Fortinet Exploitation

Investigation of Fortinet SSL-VPN vulnerability (CVE-2022-40684) exploitation attempt.
IOCs: Suspicious IPs, SSL-VPN access logs
TTPs: T1190, T1133
Containment: Blocked IPs, patched FortiOS

Darktrace Investigation

Analyzed Darktrace alerts for unusual internal network scanning and data exfiltration.
IOCs: Internal scanning IPs, unusual data transfers
TTPs: T1046, T1048
Containment: Network segmentation, blocked outbound traffic

Suspicious PowerShell Activity

Investigation of obfuscated PowerShell script attempting to download Cobalt Strike beacon.
IOCs: Base64-encoded command, known C2 IPs
TTPs: T1059.001, T1102
Containment: Isolated host, blocked domains

threat intelligence

APT29

Overview: Russian state-sponsored group (Cozy Bear).
Victims: Government, diplomatic, technology.
TTPs: T1566, T1078, T1530.

FIN7

Overview: Financially motivated cybercrime group.
Victims: Retail, hospitality, financial.
TTPs: T1059, T1071, T1046.
Detection: PowerShell download cradle, beaconing.
